name: Joash of Judah
charge: Forsaking the Lord after Jehoiada's death; stoning Zechariah in the temple court
summary: The boy king saved by the priest Jehoiada did right all the days of Jehoiada. When the priest died, the princes of Judah came and Joash hearkened to them, left the house of the Lord, and served groves and idols. Jehoiada's son Zechariah rebuked him by the Spirit; the king had him stoned in the court of the temple.
offense: Joash repaired the house of the Lord while Jehoiada lived. The collection and use of the money restored what had been damaged and returned the remaining funds to the service of the sanctuary. Yet after Jehoiada's death, the princes bowed before Joash and he listened to them. They left the Lord's house and served groves and idols. God sent prophets to bring them back, but they would not hear. When the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah, Jehoiada's son, he warned that forsaking the Lord had brought abandonment. Joash commanded that he be stoned in the court of the Lord's house. The king forgot the kindness Jehoiada had shown him and killed his son.
judgment: Wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem. A small Syrian company defeated a very great host because Judah had forsaken the Lord. The invaders destroyed the princes and sent the spoil to Damascus. They left Joash severely wounded. His servants conspired against him because of the blood of Jehoiada's sons and killed him upon his bed. He was buried in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings. The king who had repaired the sanctuary afterward shed the blood of God's witness within its court.

verses.text: And Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
Now after the death of Jehoiada came the princes of Judah, and made obeisance to the king. Then the king hearkened unto them.
And they left the house of the Lord God of their fathers, and served groves and idols: and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this their trespass.
Yet he sent prophets to them, to bring them again unto the Lord; and they testified against them: but they would not give ear.

And the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith God, Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken the Lord, he hath also forsaken you.
And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the Lord.
Thus Joash the king remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him, but slew his son. And when he died, he said, The Lord look upon it, and require it.

And it came to pass at the end of the year, that the host of Syria came up against him: and they came to Judah and Jerusalem, and destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people, and sent all the spoil of them unto the king of Damascus.

For the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men, and the Lord delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. So they executed judgment against Joash.

And when they were departed from him, (for they left him in great diseases,) his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died: and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings.
And Jehoash did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.

entries.commentary: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign and reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba. Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Most High all the days of Jehoiada the priest, because that is what he was taught. He had seen the wicked men of Israel try to kill him, so he followed the man who showed him the ropes; Jehoiada taught him how to be a righteous king and keep the commandments. A king had a job to do and could not simply sit back; he had a kingdom to watch over, and he had the priests there to help him do it.

Joash was minded to repair the house of the Most High and gathered the priests and Levites, telling them to go to the cities of Judah and gather money of all Israel to repair the house from year to year, and to hasten the matter. The Levites did not hasten it, so the king called Jehoiada the chief and asked why he had not required of the Levites the collection appointed by Moses for the tabernacle of witness. Money was needed because Israel did not let the workmen labor for nothing; when men did the jobs they were paid, for the workman is worthy of his hire, and we dealt righteously with our people. The sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God and bestowed all its dedicated things upon Baalim, which is why so much repair was needed.

At the king's commandment they made a chest and set it at the gate of the house of the Most High, and made a proclamation to bring in the collection Moses laid upon Israel in the wilderness, and the princes and people rejoiced and cast in until they made an end. Day by day the king's scribe and the high priest's officer emptied the chest and gathered money in abundance, and the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work, hiring masons, carpenters, and workers of iron and brass. Money was a defense here because it paid the skilled brothers who got the temple work done; we must deal righteously with our people today, treating a brother's business as a place to help the family and the body. Not everyone was given the same task; masons, carpenters, and metalworkers each had their charge, and every man had to listen to a manager, for business requires order and submission to authority. The workmen perfected the work and set the house of God in its state, then brought the rest of the money to make vessels of gold and silver to minister and offer with, and they offered burnt offerings continually all the days of Jehoiada. -

Jehoiada waxed old and was full of days and died, being a hundred and thirty years old at his death. They buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel both toward the Most High and toward his house. That a priest was buried among the kings shows how much respect and diligence this man had earned; his faithfulness set him alongside the rulers of the land.

After the death of Jehoiada the princes of Judah came and made obeisance to the king, and the king hearkened to them. They left the house of the Most High and served groves and idols, and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for their trespass. The Most High sent prophets to bring them again unto Him, and they testified against them, but the people would not give ear. As soon as Jehoiada died, Israel went off again, because the king was weak and started listening to those who served other gods; this teaches the lesson that lust drives Israel to idolatry, and that the Most High will always send prophets to warn them.

The spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood above the people and asked why they transgressed the commandments so that they could not prosper, telling them that because they had forsaken the Most High, He had also forsaken them. They conspired against Zechariah and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king, in the court of the house of the Most High. When the prophet came to correct the king, the king had him killed for telling him the truth; this is the same spirit our people show when a laborer brings the medicine and is met with violence. As Zechariah died he said, The Most High look upon it and require it. He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture; it is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people. -

At the end of the year the host of Syria came up against Joash, destroyed the princes of the people, and sent the spoil to the king of Damascus. The Syrians came with a small company, yet the Most High delivered a very great host of Judah into their hand, because Judah had forsaken the Most High God of their fathers; so judgment was executed on Joash for killing Zechariah. They left Joash in great diseases, and his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada and slew him on his bed, and he was buried in the city of David but not in the sepulchres of the kings. Joash began by doing right under Jehoiada's guidance, repairing the house and clearing out the idols, but none of that was remembered in the end because of the wickedness he turned to after being warned. Amaziah his son reigned in his stead; the fuller record of Joash is written in the story of the book of the kings. -

Jehoash began to reign in the seventh year of Jehu and reigned forty years in Jerusalem. He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High all the days that Jehoiada the priest instructed him. No one comes to the truth alone; the Most High set up a structure of instruction, and a person must be taught the word rather than claiming private revelation. -

Jehoash ordered that all the dedicated money brought into the house be gathered by the priests to repair the breaches of the house. But by the twenty-third year of his reign the priests still had not repaired the breaches, though he had come to power around age seven. Jehoash called Jehoiada and the priests, asked why the house was not repaired, and directed that the money no longer be received by them but delivered directly for the repairs.

Jehoiada took a chest, bored a hole in the lid, and set it beside the altar, and the priests put in all the money brought to the house. When there was much money, the king's scribe and the high priest counted it and gave it into the hands of the workmen who oversaw the repair. The money went to carpenters, builders, masons, and for timber and stone, and none was diverted to make vessels; the workmen dealt faithfully so no reckoning was needed. This is why records must be kept, especially where money is concerned; all things touching the body must be put in writing. -

Hazael king of Syria took Gath and set his face to go up against Jerusalem. Jehoash took the hallowed things dedicated by the former kings, and the gold from the treasures, and sent them to Hazael, who then went away. His own servants made a conspiracy and slew Joash in the house of Millo, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works, for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and lay them on men's shoulders, but will not move them with one of their fingers.

All their works they do for to be seen of men. They love the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the markets. He that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

Woe unto you: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men, for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. They devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer, and shall receive the greater damnation. There is a lesson in what they would not do. Where leadership provokes a man to works and he finds himself falling behind, he should take it to heart, because telling people who they are without putting in the labour yields no fruit.

They compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Their rules about swearing by the gold rather than the temple, and by the gift rather than the altar, are called out as blindness: the temple sanctifies the gold and the altar sanctifies the gift.

They pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin and have omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

They make clean the outside of the cup and platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Cleanse first that which is within. They are likened unto whited sepulchres, beautiful outward but within full of dead men's bones. Outwardly they appear righteous unto men, but within are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

They build the tombs of the prophets and say they would not have shed their blood, and by saying it they witness against themselves that they are the children of them which killed the prophets. Upon them comes all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias. This is the plainest speaking in the gospel. Christ was no soft man with these teachers of the law who did not believe it.
O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples. He gives them the words: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

The friend at midnight will not rise because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth. Importunity is persistence to the point of annoyance. The man kept knocking, and the man inside gave him enough that he would not come back.

Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. The parable before it is the point: prayer is not said once and left. There is persistence in it, and there is action behind it, because the man in the parable was standing at the door. If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
He casts out a devil, and it was dumb, and when the devil was gone out the dumb spake, and the people wondered. Others said he cast out devils through Beelzebub.

Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges. But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace; but when a stronger than he shall come upon him, he taketh from him all his armour and divideth his spoils. He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

The unclean spirit returns and finds the house swept and garnished, and takes seven other spirits more wicked than himself. The house was clean and empty. There was no stronger one dwelling in it, and that is why what came back could enter, and the last state of that man is worse than the first.
A woman blesses the womb that bare him, and he answers, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it. He turned honour away from the mother and onto the keeping of the word.

This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet. The queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and a greater than Solomon is here. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and a greater than Jonas is here. Men came a long way for less than what these would not cross the room for.

The light of the body is the eye: when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness. One lamp lights a whole room, and put out, the whole room is dark. An eye fixed on the word fills the man with light; an eye that goes looking in dark places fills the whole man, thoughts and judgments together, with darkness.

Ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness. Ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and ye are as graves which appear not.

One of the lawyers says, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also, and is answered with a woe of his own. Ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers. Ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them, so ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers. The blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, shall be required of this generation. Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
The scribes and Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him. From that point they were done with him.

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.

When a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and does according to all the abominations that the wicked do, all the righteousness which he has done shall not be remembered.
You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
